21analytics: 21 Analytics is our top Travel Rule pick for regulated VASPs, brokers and banks that must keep Travel Rule data on their own servers; it is the only interoperability partner on Coinbase's TRUST page. Its pricing page shows tiers but no prices, and G2 and Capterra list a CHF 900 monthly Starter. You run and patch the software yourself, and we found no SOC 2 report.
advance-ai: Advance.AI is an identity verification provider for businesses onboarding customers in emerging markets, strongest in Southeast Asia, with KYC, KYB, AML and credit scoring from one vendor. Prices are not published; it bills by usage, prepaid capacity or license period, and sign-up to test is free. It publishes no coverage or customer figures, so confirm country support before you commit.
aiprise: AiPrise is an identity verification provider for businesses that want KYC and KYB through one API across 200+ countries, many of them emerging markets. Prices are quoted; its own site lists none. It is young (Y Combinator, Summer 2022; $12.5M Series A in October 2025), with few public user reviews so far.
amlranger: AMLRanger is a free AI screening assistant from Ondato for quick sanctions, PEP and adverse-media checks that return short sourced reports. It is free with monthly credits, but the allowance is not published. It has no announced case management, ongoing monitoring or public API, so teams that need those should look at Ondato's main AML software.
amlwatcher: AML Watcher is an AML screening tool for small and mid-sized fintechs and payment firms that want sanctions, PEP and adverse-media checks by API or dashboard, with on-premises or in-country hosting as an option. The pricing page shows plans but no prices, and the first five searches are free. Coverage figures conflict across its own pages and there is no SOC 2 report, so ask for a written quote.
au10tix: AU10TIX is an identity verification platform for teams with steady volume that want document forensics plus a consortium of 60+ companies to catch serial and coordinated fraud. Entry plans carry a $500 monthly minimum, and per-check prices are quoted. In June 2024 it was reported that admin credentials to a logging platform had been exposed for over a year.
block-infrastructure: BlockTravel, from Block Infrastructure, is a Travel Rule API for VASPs that want Travel Rule messages and sanctions checks to run before a payment settles. There are no published prices: it is in a design partner program, with public availability planned for later in 2026. It has no public docs, named customers or certifications, and its TRP and TRISA links are confirmed only by the vendor.
blockpass: Blockpass is a Travel Rule option for small crypto firms that want customer KYC, wallet checks and Travel Rule messaging from one vendor. Plans are published from $99 a month, but its Travel Rule service, Envoy, is an unpriced add-on to the $999-a-month Corporate plan on a 12-month term. We found no TRUST, GTR, CODE or Sygna route, and its TRISA and TRP links are stated only by Blockpass.
castellum-ai: Castellum.AI is an AML screening provider for teams that want sanctions data refreshed every 5 minutes from its own database, founded by a former US Treasury official. Prices are quoted, and the contract can carry a fewer-false-positives-or-money-back guarantee. It is a screening and data specialist with a small team, not a full identity verification platform.
codevasp: CODE is a Travel Rule network for exchanges and custodians that trade with South Korean VASPs, set up in 2021 by Bithumb, Coinone and Korbit. Its Travel Rule price is not published; LEI issuance through CODE is free. It names no TRUST, TRISA or TRP route, and its ownership has shifted with its exchange shareholders.
complead: Complead, formerly Sanction Scanner, is an AML platform for teams that want screening, transaction monitoring, fraud, KYB and risk scoring on one customer record, with AI agents that triage alerts. Only the screening plan is priced, at €990 a month for 100 entities; the full platform is quoted. It does no document or biometric identity verification, so it needs an IDV partner.
complyadvantage: ComplyAdvantage is our top AML pick for teams that need sanctions, PEP and adverse-media screening on its own risk data, with agentic alert workflows. The Starter plan starts at $99 a month, and early-stage startups can apply for the free ComplyLaunch program. It does no identity verification, so you will pair it with a separate IDV provider.
complycube: ComplyCube is an eKYC API for small and mid-market teams that want document checks, biometrics and AML screening with a developer-friendly integration. Self-serve plans start at $99 a month, credited against checks. Higher tiers, NFC and video liveness are quoted, and its independent track record is thinner than the larger providers'.
cryptoswift: CryptoSwift is a hosted Travel Rule API for EU crypto firms that want prices on the website and its own STRIP network, with links through CODE and Ospree. Plans start at €600 a month on annual billing, with no setup fee. We found no TRUST or TRISA link, no counterparty is live on its TRP support yet, and the company was registered in 2023.
didit: Didit is an identity verification provider for startups, fintechs and marketplaces that want to start free and pay a public list price per module, with no minimum or contract. A full KYC check costs $0.33, and iBeta has confirmed its liveness at Level 2. The company was founded in 2023, KYB is partly priced at staging rates, and support is by email only.
enigma: Enigma is a KYB API for teams onboarding US small businesses, checking more than 100 million registrations across all 52 US jurisdictions. It costs $1.50 or $2.50 per match, with no charge when nothing matches. KYB covers the US only, so plan on another vendor for other countries.
facetec: FaceTec is a liveness and face matching provider for teams that can host it themselves, so no user data goes to FaceTec; its 3D Liveness holds iBeta and BixeLab lab letters. Prices are not published, and there is a monthly minimum. You host, scale and update the servers yourself, and it makes no ISO/IEC 27001 or SOC 2 claim.
feedzai: Feedzai is an AML and fraud platform for large banks and processors, processing about $9 trillion in payments a year in real time, by its own figures. Pricing is enterprise-only and quoted. It is built for tier-1 and tier-2 volumes, and implementation takes longer than with lighter fraud tools.
fourthline: Fourthline is an identity verification platform for regulated European financial firms such as Revolut, N26 and Bitpanda, combining identity checks, AML screening, monitoring and re-KYC. Pricing is quoted. Its merger with Veridas closed on 3 November 2026 and the platforms will be integrated in phases, so products and contracts may change.
fullcircl: FullCircl, now sold as nCino Identity Solutions, is a KYB and identity orchestration layer for regulated businesses that want 400+ verification services and registry data behind one API. Pricing is quoted. nCino retired the FullCircl brand in October 2025, so check which products and contracts carry over.
gbg: GBG is an identity verification provider for teams that need deep data infrastructure: GBG Go offers 110+ identity, fraud and risk modules across 195+ countries. Identity and fraud products are quoted; only Loqate address lookups have public prices, from 5.0p. The lineup comes from several acquisitions and can be complex to navigate.
hawkai: Hawk AI is an AML platform for banks and fintechs that want explainable AI on top of rule-based transaction monitoring, plus screening and fraud detection. Pricing is quoted. It suits mid-market and larger institutions rather than very small teams, and it does no document-based identity verification.
horuscheck: HorusCheck is a self-service KYC, KYB and AML platform with document checks, liveness, watchlist screening and a no-code flow builder. It sells pay as you go but publishes no prices. We could not confirm who runs it: the site names no company or address, so confirm the legal entity before you send it customer data.
idenfy: iDenfy is an identity verification provider for cost-conscious fintech, crypto and gaming teams, with in-house reviewers who double-check verifications around the clock. It publishes $1.35 per verification on Basic with a $135 monthly minimum, and for $0.50 more per check you pay only for approved ones. AML screening, 24/7 review and 3D liveness cost extra.
idmerit: IDMERIT is a low-cost KYC option for teams that need document and data-source checks across 180+ countries and territories from 440+ data sources. It publishes no rate card and quotes by country, module and volume; Capterra lists a start of $0.10 per user per month. In February 2026 researchers reported an unsecured database linked to IDMERIT, which the company disputes.
idnow: IDnow is an eKYC provider for firms in Germany and the DACH region that need agent-led VideoIdent built for BaFin Circular 3/2017, plus a French PVID service and qualified e-signatures. Pricing is quoted. Its case studies skew to DACH, and video checks can be slower than fully automated flows.
incode: Incode is an identity verification platform for enterprises that want onboarding and ongoing biometric authentication in one system; Gartner named it a Magic Quadrant Leader in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Pricing is enterprise-only and quoted. It costs more for smaller teams and has less AML depth than dedicated screening vendors.
iproov: iProov is a liveness provider for banks, governments and large platforms that need strong face verification inside an identity flow they already run; its Dynamic Liveness holds a FIDO certificate and iProov ID is on the UK DVS register. Prices are quoted. It sells no document checks or AML screening, and its iBeta letters date from 2020.
jumio: Jumio is an identity verification platform for high-volume enterprises, with more than 1 billion transactions processed and risk monitoring after onboarding. Rates are quoted by sales; Vendr's buyer data puts the median annual contract at about $55,850. Integration is heavier for teams without dedicated developers.
kyc360: KYC360 is an AML platform for firms with variable screening volume, now part of Experian. Ad-hoc screening is sold in search credits, from £105 a month for 21 credits. Experian is bringing it into its Ascend platform from 2026, so check which combined features are live in your market.
kycaid: KYCAID is an AML and KYC option for small and mid-market teams that want pay-per-check screening and verification with no monthly minimum. Database screening costs €0.10 a check and document verification €0.50. Its watchlist database is smaller than the leaders', and ongoing monitoring is a €100 monthly add-on.
kychub: KYC Hub is an AML platform for compliance teams that want to build onboarding, monitoring and escalation flows without code. Pricing is quoted by volume and modules, after a demo and a pilot. Its SOC 2 is described only as aligned, not as an audited report.
ledgerbrain: LedgerBrain is a wallet and transaction screening platform for VASPs that want Travel Rule messages handled in the same workspace. Screening plans start at $115 a month, but Travel Rule sits only in the custom-priced Enterprise plan. The site names no Travel Rule protocol or network, and we found no self-hosted wallet proof.
membercheck: MemberCheck is an AML screening service for sales-led compliance programs that need PEP and sanctions checks against 1,000+ watchlists, enhanced due diligence and ongoing monitoring. Pricing is quoted; transaction monitoring has a 30-day trial with 500 test credits. It publishes no hosting region, a data-residency question for some EU clients.
middesk: Middesk is a KYB provider for US fintechs, banks and lenders onboarding US businesses at volume: one call searches every Secretary of State, matches the TIN with the IRS and screens OFAC lists. Prices are quoted by sales. International checks are new and start with 30 countries on the Verify plan only.
namescan: NameScan is an AML screening tool for legal, real-estate and crypto SMEs that need one-off or batch sanctions and PEP checks without a contract. Prepaid packages start at $2.00 a scan and fall to $1.40. Ongoing monitoring sits in sister product MemberCheck, and packages expire after 12 months.
napier: Napier AI is an AML platform for financial institutions and insurers that want transaction monitoring and sanctions screening, with a sandbox to test rules before go-live. Pricing is quoted, on subscription. It does no identity verification, and its enterprise focus suits early-stage fintechs less.
nice-actimize: NICE Actimize is an AML suite for large banks that want monitoring, screening, entity risk, due diligence and regulatory reporting from one vendor. Pricing is quoted. NICE has been running a sale process for the unit since November 2025, and smaller firms may find it more than they need.
notabene: Notabene is a hosted Travel Rule network for exchanges, custodians and payment firms that want no software of their own to run. Its free plan answers incoming transfers and sends up to $10,000 a month; the full platform is quoted. TRUST works only through your own membership, and TRP is version 1.0 unless you ask for the current one.
ondato: Ondato is an identity verification provider for EU and UK businesses that want ID checks, KYB, AML screening and age checks from one vendor with prices on the page. Identity verification costs €0.50 to €1.40, but the range does not say which volume gets which price. Its liveness comes from an unnamed third party, and in July 2024 a client's data leaked from a database Ondato ran as processor.
onfido: Onfido, now sold as Entrust Identity Verification, is an identity verification platform for enterprise teams that want developer SDKs, broad document coverage and the Workflow Studio no-code builder. Pricing is quoted by sales. Support responsiveness gets mixed reviews.
ospree: Ospree is a hosted Travel Rule platform for exchanges, payment firms and OTC desks that want Travel Rule messaging and wallet screening in one API, reaching counterparties over TRISA and TRP. Prices are not published, and its three plans show the same features. It makes no SOC 2 or ISO/IEC 27001 claim and has no route to TRUST, GTR, Sygna or CODE yet.
paravision: Paravision is a liveness and face recognition supplier for companies building their own identity products, with iBeta, ACCS and DHS results behind its claims. Prices are not published. It sells no document checks or screening, and a 2021 FTC order binds the company until 2041.
persona: Persona is an identity verification platform for product teams that want to assemble their own onboarding flows from reusable document, selfie and database checks. The Essential plan starts at $250 a month on a 12-month term; larger plans are quoted. Setup takes more effort than fixed workflows, and in February 2026 its frontend code was found on a publicly reachable server.
prove: Prove is an identity verification provider for US banks, fintechs and marketplaces that want to verify customers through their phone number with few extra steps. Prices are quoted by sales; the developer sandbox is free. It runs no document, selfie or liveness checks today, so those need a second vendor.
quantexa: Quantexa is an AML platform for large banks that want entity resolution: it joins scattered data into one graph to surface hidden relationships, with HSBC, Standard Chartered and ING among its users. Pricing is quoted. The core platform needs significant data and implementation work; a separate Cloud AML product targets US mid-size and community banks.
regula: Regula is an identity verification provider for banks and border agencies that need deep document forensics, with a 16,500-template library and self-hosted options. Pricing is quoted per project, with a 30-day free trial of the Document Reader SDK. Its SDKs and readers need engineering work, and its IDV Platform with AML screening is new (October 2025).
relycomply: RelyComply is an AML platform for South African institutions under FICA that want KYC, KYB, screening, monitoring and goAML reporting in one place. Pricing is quoted. It disclosed a cyber incident in September 2026 affecting systems that hold customer data, and the forensic review was still ongoing at the latest update we found.
sanction-scanner: Sanction Scanner, now a Complead product, is an AML screening tool for mid-market teams that want sanctions, PEP and adverse-media checks without a long implementation. The Starter plan costs €990 a month for 100 entities. Its screening depth trails enterprise AML platforms, and it does no identity verification.
sardine: Sardine is an AML and fraud platform for financial institutions and larger platforms that want fraud scoring from device and behavior signals next to monitoring, screening and case management. Pricing is quoted. It is not a document-first identity verification platform and is not built for small teams.
seon: SEON is a fraud and AML platform for teams that want to score risk from email, phone, IP and device data before a user submits an ID. The Starter plan costs $699 a month for 2,500 fraud checks, without AML screening or case management. Its own document and liveness checks only launched in January 2026, starting in Europe.
shufti-pro: Shufti Pro is our top identity verification pick for teams that need coverage of 240+ countries and territories and a choice of SaaS, private cloud or on-premise deployment. A free tier covers 10 verifications a month, and Essentials starts at $1.50 per verification. Enterprise volumes are quoted, and its certifications page names no ISO 27001 certification body.
signicat: Signicat is an eKYC provider for pan-European onboarding, with 35+ mostly European eID methods and wallets, VideoID and e-signing from an EU qualified trust service provider. Pricing is quoted, with setup, subscription and transaction fees and a free developer account. Its strength is concentrated in Europe, and products from many acquisitions can feel less unified.
signzy: Signzy is an eKYC provider for Indian banks and financial firms that need Aadhaar checks, CKYC and RBI-compliant V-CIP video KYC in a no-code journey builder. Pricing is pay as you go by API and quoted. Outside India it needs more configuration, and a cyberattack at Signzy was reported in December 2024.
smartsearch: SmartSearch is an AML verification service for UK legal, property, accountancy and financial firms, with individual and business checks and a DIATF-certified SmartDoc identity check. Pricing is quoted; three tiers are listed without prices. Its product and clients centre on the UK.
socure: Socure is an identity verification provider for US consumer onboarding, checking a person's details, phone and email against identity data before asking for a document. Self-serve plans cost $0.80 to $1.30 per evaluation, with $1,000 of free credits a month. Its liveness claim has no published iBeta letter, and KYB relies on partner data.
strise: Strise is an AML platform for Nordic banks and insurers that want AI to automate routine compliance work, built on a knowledge graph of companies, owners, sanctions and adverse media. Pricing is usage-based and quoted. It is a smaller company ($10.8M Series A in 2023) whose customers are mostly Nordic.
sumsub: Sumsub is an identity verification platform for crypto and fintech teams that want ID checks, AML screening and the Travel Rule from one vendor at published prices. Plans start at $1.35 a verification with a $149 monthly minimum; KYB and transaction monitoring are quoted separately. One caution: Sumsub disclosed a support-system breach in February 2026.
trp: TRP, at travel-rule.com, is a hosted Travel Rule API for smaller VASPs and is not the open Travel Rule Protocol. A €2,000 deposit becomes your message balance, then self-hosted wallet messages cost €0.02 each. The site names no legal entity or certifications, and the docs show no connection to other Travel Rule networks.
trulioo: Trulioo is an identity verification provider for teams that need data-source checks on people and businesses across 195 countries, with KYB and screening against 6,000+ watchlists. Prices are quoted. It is a data API that needs technical resources to integrate, not a no-code platform.
unit21: Unit21 is an AML and fraud platform for regulated financial institutions that want AI agents to triage alerts, gather evidence and pre-fill SARs, with Chime, Green Dot and Sallie Mae among its customers. Pricing is not published. Its CEO changed in April 2026, when co-founder Trisha Kothari moved to chair.
veridas: Veridas is an identity verification provider for teams in Spain, Latin America and Europe that want in-house facial and voice biometrics, with liveness that passed iBeta ISO 30107-3 testing. Pricing is quoted. It merged into Fourthline on 3 November 2026, so product and brand changes are likely.
veriff: Veriff is an identity verification provider for teams that want automated decisions backed by human review, with iBeta Level 2 liveness and a UK DIATF-certified service. Self-serve plans start at $0.80 per verification with a $49 monthly minimum. In November 2025 an intruder took ID images of 8,583 Total Wireless customers from Veriff's systems.
verified: Verified is an eKYC provider for Nordic B2B firms that want AML and KYC screening, e-signing and digital identification in one system. Prices are not published; it quotes after a demo. Its reach outside the Nordics is limited, and there are few public user reviews.
verifymy: VerifyMy is an age verification provider for platforms with age-gating duties, offering email-based age estimation next to mobile, card, facial and ID document checks, certified to ISO/IEC 27566-1. Prices are not published. It is not a general KYC or AML platform, and public user reviews are few.
verifyvasp: VerifyVASP is a members-only Travel Rule network for firms whose counterparties are mostly in Asia-Pacific, above all South Korea, Singapore and, since it bought Sygna in April 2026, Japan. Prices are not published; it charges a subscription plus API usage. Its SOC 2 Type II claim names no auditor, and we found no TRUST, TRP or GTR link.
vespia: Vespia is a KYB platform, now part of Veriff, that pulls company register data from 300+ jurisdictions with AI assistance. Its Starter package costs €99 and KYB reports start at €35, priced by region. Sign-up now redirects to Veriff, so evaluate it as part of Veriff.
width: WIDTH is a compliance platform for firms in Singapore and Asia-Pacific that want Travel Rule messaging next to KYC, wallet screening and case management. Platform plans start at $1,499 a year, but Travel Rule is quoted after a demo. None of the networks it names lists WIDTH, and the company was registered in January 2026.
yoti: Yoti is an age verification provider for platforms that must check age at scale, with ten methods behind one integration and an iBeta Level 3 liveness letter. An age check costs £0.15, with a £15 monthly minimum. Spain's data protection authority fined it €950,000 in March 2026 over its Digital ID app; Yoti is appealing.
zyphe: Zyphe is a KYB and KYC option for smaller fintech, crypto and iGaming teams that want a cheap self-serve rate card and AI agents that prepare reviews. ID and liveness cost $0.30 a check, after a $25 sign-up credit. It is very young: SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001 audits are still in progress, and its liveness has no published lab test.
